hook: Nine days on, Ubuntu still had no fix.

beats.say: On November 16th, details of NoisyTCP, a remote memory corruption flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP stack, were published. Nine days later, Ubuntu had not published a fix.
Other distributions had a fix ready when the details were published, and a KVM host escape affecting AMD virtualization, disclosed November 18th, had no Ubuntu fix.
The author argues remote kernel flaws need updates within hours, not days or weeks, and notes Ubuntu backports patches to an older kernel instead of tracking long-term releases.
